transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Because water is on the floor next to live plug sockets, this is an electrical hazard. Do not use the appliance or touch the sockets until a qualified engineer has checked them for safety. Regarding the leak: common causes are a damaged door seal, something caught in it, or items in the racks deflecting spray out of the door. Less commonly, water may be leaking internally from a pump or hose and pooling underneath. To help narrow this down safely (with the machine off), please check if the rubber door seal is intact and clear of debris, and ensure nothing in the racks is blocking the spray arms.
its still running tho!! the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. the door seal looks ok. what do i do

You must switch off the power at the consumer unit immediately and do not touch the appliance or the extension lead. Because water is spreading towards live electrical equipment, this is a serious shock hazard that requires a qualified electrician to check your sockets before the machine can be used again. Regarding the leak: since the door seal looks fine, the most likely cause is an internal failure, such as a split hose or a leaking pump seal inside the base of the dishwasher. This is not something you can safely fix yourself without dismantling the unit and dealing with electrical components near water. Please call a qualified appliance engineer to repair the leak and have an electrician verify your socket safety.
